name: Garba — do taali (two claps)
summary: The two-clap Garba basic: step, step, clap — the circle step everyone starts with.
setup: Face the phone about 2.5 m away, camera at hip height, whole body and both arms in frame. Step to the side, bring the other foot behind, dip slightly and clap at chest height. Keep the rhythm even and stay light on the feet.
brief: Step to the side, bring the other foot behind, dip slightly and clap. Keep the rhythm even and stay light on the feet.
why: The hands coming together is the clearest thing in the frame from the front, so the claps are counted. The footwork pattern and the travel around the circle are yours to watch.
calibrationPose: Standing with the hands apart at chest height, before the first clap.
tempo: Start at a walking pace; speed up over the set as Garba does.
progression: Faster tempo; deeper dip; add the tran taali (three-clap) pattern.
contraindications: Knee pain on the dip; ankle or foot pain from repeated bouncing on a hard floor.

faults.label: Staying upright and stiff
faults.cue: Bend the knees — dip with the clap
faults.tip: Garba is a soft, bouncing step. Locked knees turn it into marching and jar the joints.

faults.label: Hands barely meeting
faults.tip: Open the arms out and bring them together at chest height. Small hand flicks lose the rhythm.

faults.label: Stamping flat-footed
faults.tip: Landing flat on a hard floor for several minutes is what makes the calves and shins sore afterwards.

faults.label: Rounding the shoulders
faults.tip: Long sets tire the upper back and the shoulders creep forward. Keep the chest lifted.

faults.label: Rhythm drifting
faults.tip: The step is on the beat and the clap on the count. Drifting turns the circle into a shuffle.

guide.surface: Any floor with a little give. Barefoot or soft shoes; a hard floor for long sets is what makes feet ache.
guide.stop: Knee pain on the dip, or shin pain that builds.
guide.cannotSee: The footwork pattern, the direction of travel and the turn of the wrists.

points.t: Step to the side, other foot behind, soft landings.
Stay light — the heel touches, it does not stamp.
Open wide, then clap at chest height on the count.
